flashcard_questions.q: What is a pure substance in chemistry?
flashcard_questions.a: A substance containing only one element or one compound.

flashcard_questions.q: How can a melting point show that a substance is impure?
flashcard_questions.a: It melts over a range of temperatures, not sharply.

flashcard_questions.q: Pure water melts at exactly ____ and boils at exactly ____.
What is a formulation in chemistry?
flashcard_questions.a: A mixture designed with components in precise quantities to give specific properties.

flashcard_questions.q: In paper chromatography, what is the mobile phase?
flashcard_questions.a: The solvent that moves up through the paper.

flashcard_questions.q: In paper chromatography, what is the stationary phase?
Why is the start line on a chromatogram drawn in pencil?
flashcard_questions.a: Pencil marks are insoluble, so they will not dissolve in the solvent.

flashcard_questions.q: How many spots does a pure substance produce on a chromatogram?
Rf = distance moved by substance ÷ distance moved by ____.
What is the range of possible Rf values?
Which gas burns with a squeaky pop when a burning splint is held to it?
Which gas relights a glowing splint?
What happens to limewater when carbon dioxide is bubbled through it?
flashcard_questions.a: It turns cloudy, or milky white.

flashcard_questions.q: What does chlorine gas do to damp litmus paper?
Why is 'it puts out a flame' not the accepted test for carbon dioxide?
flashcard_questions.a: Many other gases also put out a flame.
